1.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V3 and v11 keep the KJV's LORD of hosts, explained as (armies).

verses.text: Now there was a certain man of Ramathaimzophim, of mount Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephrathite.
And Elkanah had 2 wives. The name of the one was Hannah, and the name of the other Peninnah. And Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.
And this man went up out of his city yearly to worship and to sacrifice to the LORD of hosts (armies) in Shiloh. And the 2 sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, the priests of the LORD, were there.
And when the time was that Elkanah offered, he gave to Peninnah his wife, and to all her sons and her daughters, portions (shares of the meat).
But to Hannah he gave a worthy (double) portion, for he loved Hannah. But the LORD had shut up her womb (she could not have children).
And her adversary (rival) also provoked her sore (upset her very much), to make her fret (feel bad), because the LORD had shut up her womb.
And as Elkanah did so year by year, when Hannah went up to the house of the LORD, so Peninnah provoked (upset) her. Therefore Hannah wept, and did not eat.
Then Elkanah her husband said to her: Hannah, why do you weep? And why do you not eat? And why is your heart grieved (sad)? Am I not better to you than 10 sons?
So Hannah rose up after they had eaten in Shiloh, and after they had drunk. Now Eli the priest sat upon a seat by a post of the temple of the LORD.
And Hannah was in bitterness of soul (deeply hurt), and prayed to the LORD, and wept sore (very much).

And Hannah vowed a vow (made a serious promise), and said: O LORD of hosts (armies), if You will indeed look on the affliction (suffering) of Your handmaid (servant), and remember me, and not forget Your handmaid (servant), but will give to Your handmaid (servant) a man child, then I will give him to the LORD all the days of his life, and there shall no razor come upon his head.
And it came to pass, as Hannah continued praying before the LORD, that Eli marked (watched) her mouth.
Now Hannah, she spoke in her heart. Only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard. Therefore Eli thought she had been drunken.
And Eli said to her: How long will you be drunken? Put away your wine from you.
And Hannah answered and said: No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit. I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the LORD.
Count not your handmaid (servant) for a daughter of Belial (a worthless woman). For out of the abundance (greatness) of my complaint and grief have I spoken until now.
Then Eli answered and said: Go in peace. And the God of Israel grant you your petition (request) that you have asked of Him.
And Hannah said: Let your handmaid (servant) find grace (favor) in your sight. So the woman went her way, and did eat, and her countenance (face) was no more sad.
And they rose up in the morning early, and worshipped before the LORD, and returned, and came to their house to Ramah. And Elkanah knew (lay with) Hannah his wife. And the LORD remembered her.

Therefore it came to pass, when the time was come about after Hannah had conceived (become pregnant), that she bare (gave birth to) a son, and called his name Samuel, saying: Because I have asked him of the LORD.
And the man Elkanah, and all his house (family), went up to offer to the LORD the yearly sacrifice, and his vow (promised gift).

But Hannah went not up. For she said to her husband: I will not go up until the child be weaned (done nursing), and then I will bring him, so that he may appear before the LORD, and there abide (stay) for ever.

And Elkanah her husband said to her: Do what seems good to you. Tarry (stay) until you have weaned (finished nursing) him. Only the LORD establish (keep) His word. So the woman abode (stayed), and gave her son suck (nursed him) until she weaned (finished nursing) him.

And when Hannah had weaned (finished nursing) him, she took him up with her, with 3 bullocks (young bulls), and one ephah (about 5 gallons) of flour, and a bottle of wine, and brought him to the house of the LORD in Shiloh. And the child was young.
And they slew (killed) a bullock (young bull), and brought the child to Eli.
And Hannah said: Oh my lord, as your soul lives, my lord, I am the woman that stood by you here, praying to the LORD.
For this child I prayed. And the LORD has given me my petition (request) which I asked of Him.
Therefore also I have lent him to the LORD. As long as he lives he shall be lent to the LORD. And Samuel worshipped the LORD there.

5.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. The ark is written the ark (holy box), and the KJV's emerods are explained as (painful sores).

verses.text: And the Philistines took the ark (holy box) of God, and brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.
When the Philistines took the ark (holy box) of God, they brought it into the house of Dagon (their false god), and set it by Dagon.

And when the people of Ashdod arose (got up) early on the morrow (next day), look, Dagon was fallen upon his face to the earth before the ark (holy box) of the LORD. And they took Dagon, and set him in his place again.

And when they arose (got up) early on the morrow (next) morning, look, Dagon was fallen upon his face to the ground before the ark (holy box) of the LORD. And the head of Dagon and both the palms of his hands were cut off upon the threshold (doorstep). Only the stump of Dagon was left to him.
Therefore neither the priests of Dagon, nor any that come into Dagon's house, tread on the threshold (doorstep) of Dagon in Ashdod to this day.
But the hand of the LORD was heavy upon them of Ashdod, and He destroyed them, and smote (struck) them with emerods (painful sores), even Ashdod and the coasts (land around) of it.
And when the men of Ashdod saw that it was so, they said: The ark (holy box) of the God of Israel shall not abide (stay) with us. For His hand is sore (hard) upon us, and upon Dagon our god.

They sent therefore and gathered all the lords (rulers) of the Philistines to them, and said: What shall we do with the ark (holy box) of the God of Israel? And they answered: Let the ark (holy box) of the God of Israel be carried about to Gath. And they carried the ark (holy box) of the God of Israel about there.

And it was so, that, after they had carried it about, the hand of the LORD was against the city with a very great destruction. And He smote (struck) the men of the city, both small and great, and they had emerods (painful sores) in their secret parts.

Therefore they sent the ark (holy box) of God to Ekron. And it came to pass, as the ark (holy box) of God came to Ekron, that the Ekronites cried out, saying: They have brought about the ark (holy box) of the God of Israel to us, to slay (kill) us and our people.

So they sent and gathered together all the lords (rulers) of the Philistines, and said: Send away the ark (holy box) of the God of Israel, and let it go again to its own place, so that it slay (kill) us not, and our people. For there was a deadly destruction throughout all the city. The hand of God was very heavy there.
And the men that died not were smitten (struck) with the emerods (painful sores). And the cry of the city went up to heaven.

16.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version, checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V7 keeps the KJV's man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart. V14-16 and v23 keep the KJV's evil spirit from the LORD/God.

verses.text: And the LORD said to Samuel: How long will you mourn for Saul, seeing I have rejected him from reigning (ruling) over Israel? Fill your horn with oil, and go. I will send you to Jesse the Bethlehemite. For I have provided Me a king among his sons.
And Samuel said: How can I go? If Saul hear it, he will kill me. And the LORD said: Take an heifer (young cow) with you, and say: I am come to sacrifice to the LORD.
And call Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will show you what you shall do. And you shall anoint (pour oil on) for Me him whom I name to you.
And Samuel did that which the LORD spoke, and came to Bethlehem. And the elders of the town trembled (shook) at his coming, and said: Do you come peaceably?

And Samuel said: Peaceably. I am come to sacrifice to the LORD. Sanctify (make clean and holy) yourselves, and come with me to the sacrifice. And Samuel sanctified (made holy) Jesse and his sons, and called them to the sacrifice.
And it came to pass, when they were come, that Samuel looked on Eliab, and said: Surely the LORD's anointed (chosen one) is before Him.

But the LORD said to Samuel: Look not on his countenance (face), or on the height of his stature (how tall he is), because I have refused him. For the LORD sees not as man sees. For man looks on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart.
Then Jesse called Abinadab, and made him pass before Samuel. And Samuel said: Neither has the LORD chosen this one.
Then Jesse made Shammah to pass by. And Samuel said: Neither has the LORD chosen this one.
Again, Jesse made 7 of his sons to pass before Samuel. And Samuel said to Jesse: The LORD has not chosen these.

And Samuel said to Jesse: Are here all your children? And Jesse said: There remains yet the youngest, and look, he keeps the sheep. And Samuel said to Jesse: Send and fetch (bring) him. For we will not sit down till he come here.

And Jesse sent, and brought him in. Now David was ruddy (healthy and red-cheeked), and with a beautiful countenance (face), and goodly (handsome) to look to. And the LORD said: Arise (get up), anoint (pour oil on) him. For this is he.

Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed (poured oil on) David in the middle of his brethren (brothers). And the Spirit of the LORD came upon David from that day forward. So Samuel rose up, and went to Ramah.
But the Spirit of the LORD departed (left) from Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD troubled him.
And Saul's servants said to him: Look now, an evil spirit from God troubles you.

Let our lord now command your servants, which are before you, to seek out a man, who is a cunning (skillful) player on an harp. And it shall come to pass, when the evil spirit from God is upon you, that he shall play with his hand, and you shall be well.
And Saul said to his servants: Provide (find) me now a man that can play well, and bring him to me.

Then one of the servants answered, and said: Look, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite, that is cunning (skillful) in playing, and a mighty valiant (brave) man, and a man of war, and prudent (wise) in matters, and a comely (handsome) person, and the LORD is with him.
Therefore Saul sent messengers to Jesse, and said: Send me David your son, which is with the sheep.
And Jesse took an ass (donkey) laden (loaded) with bread, and a bottle of wine, and a kid (young goat), and sent them by David his son to Saul.
And David came to Saul, and stood before him. And Saul loved David greatly. And David became his armourbearer (the one who carried his armor).
And Saul sent to Jesse, saying: Let David, I pray you (please), stand before me. For he has found favour in my sight.
And it came to pass, when the evil spirit from God was upon Saul, that David took an harp, and played with his hand. So Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit departed (left) from him.
